feedback: If the learner thinks the draw-back is a chance to explore or collect shells: explain the draw-back means much more water is coming — it is the signal to flee to high ground.
If the learner assumes one wave: tsunamis often arrive as a series; later waves can be larger, so stay away until officials say it is safe.
A safety card can snap up when the draw-back happens ('sea pulling back means run to high ground') to make the rule memorable.
activities.intendedInsight: A receding shoreline is a natural warning sign of an approaching tsunami; the correct, empowering response is to move immediately to high ground, not to explore the exposed sea bed. The sea does not always pull back first, so strong shaking near the coast or an official warning also means go to high ground.
learnerActions: Watch the shoreline just before the surge arrives: in this example the water races OUT, exposing the sea bed, before flooding back in (this often happens, but not with every tsunami).
Answer: 'If you were at the beach and the sea suddenly pulled far back, exposing the sand, what would that mean and what would you do?'
Learn and repeat the safety rule: sea pulling back = get to high ground quickly; do not walk out onto the newly exposed sand.
Note that a tsunami can arrive as several waves, and later ones can be larger — it is not safe once the first wave passes.
activities.title: The sea pulls back: a warning to run

feedback: If the learner becomes anxious: emphasise the safety-empowering framing — warning systems and knowing what to do greatly reduce the danger.
Check the retell includes both the cause (sea-floor movement) and the warning (draw-back → high ground).
activities.intendedInsight: Tsunamis are real natural hazards, but people are not helpless: understanding the cause, recognising warning signs, and warning systems all help keep people safe.
learnerActions: Hear or read a brief, age-appropriate account of a real tsunami to understand that this really happens, without dwelling on distressing detail.
Discuss what people now do to stay safe: warning systems exist, and the natural signs (the sea drawing back, strong shaking near the coast) can give time to move.
Retell the causal chain and the safety rule to a partner or adult as if explaining it to someone who has never heard of a tsunami.
activities.title: Make it real: a told account and warning systems
